# Freemap.sk

> Freemap.sk is a web map application built on OpenStreetMap data by the NGO Freemap Slovakia (a Slovak local chapter of the OpenStreetMap Foundation). Most of it is free to use; an optional paid premium tier funds the service and unlocks extras. Its focus is a detailed outdoor map for hiking, cycling, cross-country skiing and horse riding across Europe, complemented by many additional base and overlay layers and by tools for search, route planning, drawing and measurement, GPX viewing, live tracking, personal maps, map embedding, and export. This file gives AI systems and assistants structured information so they can explain, describe, and help users interact with the site.

Contact: [info@freemap.sk](mailto:info@freemap.sk)

Key facts:

- Built on OpenStreetMap data; the map is continuously updated from the OSM database.
- Most of the app is free to use. An optional yearly premium tier (15 €) and prepaid credits unlock extras: high-resolution elevation data, the finer panorama and viewshed renders, most colorize modes, and premium photos.
- Displays marked hiking, biking, skiing and riding trails, and supports high-resolution (retina) displays.
- Background and overlay layers include the NLC forest roads, aerial imagery, public transport, Wikipedia, community photos, and an animated weather radar.
- Tools: search (by name or category), route planning (walking, cycling, stroller, wheelchair, car, skiing, etc.), map annotation (points, lines, polygons), measurement (distance, elevation, area, position), GPX track viewing, personal saved maps, live tracking, and export (GPX, GeoJSON, KML/KMZ, PDF, SVG, PNG, WebP, JPG).
- Users can generate embed code to place the map on their own websites.
- The application is a single-page application (SPA) and reflects its state in the URL.

Only the summary and the deep-link reference are in this file. Everything else — the application's functions (the main-menu tools and modals) and the available map layers — is in the reference files listed below, one fetch each.

## Deep links (building map URLs)

The app keeps its state in the URL, so you can hand a user a link that opens Freemap in a specific state — a viewport, chosen layers, markers, drawn lines/areas, a planned route, or an opened modal — with no API and no login. This is the normal way to "create a map" programmatically: build the URL and give it to the user.

Parameters live in the URL **hash** (`#name=value&name2=value2…`); a query string (`?name=…`) is accepted as a fallback. Base URL: `https://www.freemap.sk/`.

The highest-value parameters for building links:

- `map=zoom/lat/lon` — viewport, e.g. `map=13/48.7483/19.1480` (coordinates to 6 decimals). With a fractional **Zoom step**, the zoom can be fractional too, to 2 decimals (`map=13.75/…`).
- `layers=codes` — base layer + overlays by their id code (see the layer registry in [Map Layers](/llms-layers.md)), e.g. `layers=X` (Outdoor) or `layers=X~I` (Outdoor + Photos).
- `as-overlay=codes`, `as-base=codes` — WMS, shading or raster tile maps shown as the other kind than their own (e.g. `layers=X~WKA&as-overlay=WKA` lays the cadastre over Outdoor); written only for a map switched in Installed maps or its panel.
- **`point=lat/lon` — put a marker on the map. This is the parameter for "a map with points / markers". It is repeatable: add one `point=` per marker.**
- `line=lat/lon,lat/lon,…` and `polygon=lat/lon,lat/lon,…` — draw a line or a filled area (each repeatable).
- `points=[transport/]lat/lon,…` together with `transport=…` — a **planned route** through waypoints. This is routing, not standalone markers — do not confuse the plural `points=` with the marker parameter `point=`.
- `show=type[/arg]` — open a modal/viewer, e.g. `show=gallery-viewer/123`.
- `elevation-chart=feature` — open the elevation profile on the feature named: `route-planner` (the planned route), `track-viewer` (the active imported track), `tracking/<deviceToken>` (a tracked device), or `drawing/<lineIndex>` (a drawn line, by its zero-based `line=`/`polygon=` index). Only one profile shows at a time, and it opens once the geometry it charts has loaded — so it can be combined with `points=`, `track-uid=`, `import-url=` or a saved map's `id=`.
- `elevation-chart-range=<from>,<to>` — the stretch of that profile marked out for its own figures, in whole metres along it. Ignored without an `elevation-chart=`, and dropped where the profile turns out shorter than it.
- `route-colorize-by=mode`, `track-colorize-by=mode`, `tracking-colorize-by=mode` — what the planned route, the loaded track, or the tracked devices are colored by: `elevation`, `steepness`, `surface`, `smoothness`, `roadType`, `trackType`, `hikeRating`, `mtbRating`, `trailColor`, `speed`, `heartRate`, `cadence`, `power`, `temperature`, `time`, `heading`, `battery`, `gsmSignal`. A mode the feature has no data for simply paints nothing, and an unknown name is ignored. Since the elevation profile takes its colors from the same setting, this colors the chart too.
- `route-colorize-legend=1|0`, `track-colorize-legend=1|0`, `tracking-colorize-legend=1|0` — whether that feature's legend, the box naming what the colors mean, is shown. Written only alongside a mode, since the legend appears only while one is active; omitted, the reader's own preference stands (it defaults to shown).
- `route-params-hash=key` — carries a **premium route feature to someone without premium**: multimodal segmentation, and the premium colorize modes. It is the key of the route the link was made for, so it applies to that route alone and lapses as soon as a waypoint moves — the reader sees the feature on the shared route, never on one of their own. Written only while the route already has those features (a premium user's, or a shared one being passed on), so a link cannot be made to grant what its author did not have.
- `lang=code` — force the UI language (`en`, `sk`, …).

**Example — a map with two markers** (Bratislava and Košice) on the Outdoor layer:

```
https://www.freemap.sk/#map=8/48.43/19.18&layers=X&point=48.14816/17.10674&point=48.72083/21.25808
```

**Styling, labelling and opening the editor.** After the `lat/lon`, a `point` / `line` / `polygon` value may carry style fields, each a one-letter code, joined by the record-separator `%1E` (a leading `%1E` separates them from the coordinates). The useful codes are `L`abel, `C`olor (`%23` = `#`, RGBA hex), `S`hape (`s`quare / `r`ing, default pin), and `I`con spec — `poi:<name>` for a bundled POI icon or `fa:<name>` for a Font Awesome icon (`%3A` = `:`). The markers show on their own; `tools=draw-points` is optional and only additionally opens the drawing toolbar so the user can edit the points. E.g. a blue ring marker labelled "Ahoj!" with the animal-shelter icon:

```
https://www.freemap.sk/#map=17/48.979457/21.169961&layers=X&tools=draw-points&point=48.979061/21.167738%1EC%230000ff%1ELAhoj!%1ESr%1EIpoi%3Aanimal_shelter
```

For every URL parameter and the full style codec, see [`doc/url-params.md`](https://github.com/FreemapSlovakia/freemap-v3-react/blob/main/doc/url-params.md).

## Reference files

Each is a Markdown fragment of this document, continuing its heading levels. Together they describe every function and map layer. The functions are reached from the main menu, under a button with a "hamburger" icon at the top left of the page.

- [Interface, search and account](/llms-interface.md): the search box (places, coordinates, OSM elements, the app's own functions), the UI language and theme switchers, the account with purchases, premium, credits and login providers, clearing the map, the help documents and legend, and the map context menu.
- [Photos and personal maps](/llms-photos-maps.md): the community photo layer, uploading and rating photos, the leaderboard, and saved personal maps (sharing, offline flagging, writing back).
- [Drawing and measurement](/llms-drawing.md): drawing points, lines and polygons, their styles and labels, distance, area, elevation and position measurement, and the elevation profile of a drawn line.
- [Routes and tracks](/llms-routes-tracks.md): the route finder (transport modes, waypoints, alternatives, isochrones, colorizing, elevation profile) and imported tracks and data files (GPX, GeoJSON, KML/KMZ, TCX, …).
- [OpenStreetMap objects, details and changes](/llms-osm.md): searching POIs by category, the map-details panel for an OSM element, and the recent-changes viewer.
- [Live tracking and the GPS recorder](/llms-tracking.md): tracked devices, watched devices, access tokens, and the standalone Android GPS recorder the app drives.
- [Toposcope and panorama](/llms-views.md): the printable direction dial of surrounding summits, and the 360° terrain render with its peak names, distances and quality steps.
- [Offline use](/llms-offline.md): what works without a connection and where settings are kept, downloaded offline maps, and caching tiles while browsing.
- [Sharing and export](/llms-export.md): sharing a link or opening the place in another app, exporting the map as an image or document, exporting map data, maps for GPS devices, exporting an offline map, and the embed code.
- [Map Layers](/llms-layers.md): the map toolbar and the full layer registry with each layer's id code, zoom range, coverage and credits.
- [Manage maps](/llms-manage-maps.md): Installed maps (each map's toolbar, menu, opacity and shortcut settings) and Available maps (searching, previewing and installing maps), custom maps and combinations, map and elevation preferences.
- [In-page agent tools (WebMCP)](/llms-agent-tools.md): the tools the app registers on `document.modelContext` for an AI agent running in the user's browser.
